_comment: DriverAI Hiring Auto-Reply - the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the PA flow. Edit values here, run 'python build_zip.py', then re-import the .zip in Power Automate. Do NOT hand-edit definition.json - build_zip.py regenerates it from this file. Keys starting with '_' are comments and are ignored by the builder.
_comment_interval: trigger.interval_min sets how often the inbox is polled. It only takes effect after re-importing the rebuilt zip - Power Automate cannot change a trigger interval at runtime.
_comment_loopguard: Self-loop protection is SENDER-based: apply@driverai.io (plus mailer-daemon/postmaster/bounce) is in bad_senders, so the flow never answers itself or a bounce. Outbound subjects are NOT added to bad_subjects - that would drop applicants' 'Re: <our subject>' replies before the reference gate. Per-applicant caps stop any runaway loop. List only the junk subjects you want blocked in bad_subjects.
_comment_flowname: flow_name sets the package display name (shown when importing) AND the flow display name. build_zip.py writes it into the package manifest + definition. For a brand-new import it names the flow; for an Update import PA keeps the existing flow's name but the package name is fixed.
_comment_testmode: test_mode.suppress_emails=true replaces every applicant-facing Send_* action AND Notify_failure with a no-op Compose (same runAfter wiring, so tidy/patch sequencing is untouched) - used for a historical-replay test so reprocessing old mail never actually emails anyone. Mail Sent/Decline Sent stamps also switch to a 'TEST-MODE (suppressed) <timestamp>' marker instead of 'Sent <timestamp>' so replayed rows are visibly distinguishable later. MUST be set back to false, rebuilt, and re-imported to restore live behavior when the test is done.
_comment_rules: Caps share ONE 'Application Updates' column on the candidate's row. A no-CV application is replied to (Email 3) but NOT written to SharePoint, so it has no row and no cap. duplicate_check_days = the resubmit window; the *_max values are the OVERALL cap (Application Updates keeps counting up to this, then the row goes fully silent forever within the 90-day window). reply_cap is a SEPARATE, smaller threshold: contacts up to reply_cap still get an actual reply email (the last one, at reply_cap, is the final-notice); contacts between reply_cap and *_max still update the row/resume (re-queued for P2) but get NO email at all - 'no other reminders'.
_comment_dated: dated_resume_subfolders=true files each resume under resumes_folder/<Year>/<Month>/ (e.g. .../2026/June/). The candidate workbook is stored separately under Master_Files so the resume tree contains only resume files. Phase 2 reconstructs the same resume path from the row's Received Date. Set false to save resumes flat in resumes_folder.
_comment_libid: documents_library_id is the SharePoint 'Documents' library's internal list GUID on this site. The CreateNewFolder operation (workbook self-heal) needs it as a separate 'List or Library' selector - it does NOT accept the folder path alone. Find it in an existing CreateNewFolder/CreateFile action's 'table'/'List or Library' picker if you move tenants.
_comment_selfheal: The workbook is NO LONGER auto-created or overwritten (changed 2026-07-04). The old metadata probe was unreliable (false NotFound) and its self-heal re-uploaded a blank template over real data, wiping rows. Now: if the workbook is genuinely missing, the run fails and Notify_failure alerts the admin so a human restores it once from P1_Templates/HiringAgent_P1_CandidateList.xlsx - never silently replaced. Dated resume folders ARE still auto-created (safe no-op if they exist). No self-heal delays: PA Consumption requires any Wait to be 5s..30d, and testing showed the folder->file save works with no delay, so the delays were removed. If a propagation-lag issue ever reappears, re-add a Wait of AT LEAST 5 seconds (below 5s fails with BadRequest).
_comment_excel: Excel Online (Business) addressing used by Get/Add row actions. 'source' = the SharePoint site id triple (host,siteId,webId); 'drive' = document library drive id; 'file' = workbook path; 'table' = table name. Find these in an existing Get/Add-row action if you move tenants.
_comment_tidy: inbox_tidy: after the flow finishes handling an email it is moved out of the Inbox (MoveV2). TWO destinations by category: (1) LEGITIMATE application mail (new CV, non-CV request, duplicate, wrong-format, update, follow-up, ignored) is marked READ (MarkAsRead_V3) and moved to `destination` (Archive) - so Archive holds only real application traffic. (2) SPAM/JUNK caught by the 3 gates (bad sender, bad subject, scam/malware/phishing/offensive/foreign) is moved to `spam_destination` (Junk Email) and left UNREAD (just moved, not marked read) so it stands out as junk. For built-in well-known folders use the connector's CAPITALIZED friendly name ('Archive', 'Junk Email', 'Deleted Items') - casing matters. For a custom folder use its mail-folder ID from Graph Explorer. Set enabled=false to leave everything unread in the Inbox (safe - the trigger watermark prevents reprocessing).
_comment_year_separator: When enabled, the FIRST new-applicant row of each calendar year gets one blank row inserted into CandidateList immediately before it (only on the brand-new-applicant path - never on duplicate/update/follow-up, which only PATCH an existing row). Detected via a cheap server-side Excel $filter for 'any row with Received Date >= <thisYear>-01-01' - bounded to just this year's volume, never a full-table scan, so it stays cheap as the table grows across years. Purely visual/organizational (lets a human scrolling the sheet see where one year's entries end and the next begin) - does not affect duplicate detection, scoring, or any other logic, since P1/P2 both already skip fully-blank rows when reading. Best-effort: if P1 is ever down across the exact New Year's boundary, whichever new-applicant row happens to trigger the check first still inserts the separator right before itself, just not necessarily before the very first 2027 row if others already landed. Set enabled=false to turn this off entirely.
_comment_month_separator: Same idea as year_separator but per calendar MONTH: the FIRST new-applicant row of each month gets one blank row inserted before it. Detected with a bounded server-side $filter over that month only (Received Date ge <first of month> and lt <first of next month>), so it never scans the whole table. IMPORTANT: at a January boundary the year separator already fires, and two blank rows in a row would look like a mistake - so the month check deliberately requires 'no rows this month AND at least one row already this year', which makes the year separator win and keeps exactly ONE blank row at any boundary. Same best-effort caveat as year_separator if P1 is down across a month boundary. Purely visual: P1 and P2 both skip fully-blank rows when reading. Set enabled=false to turn off.
_comment_appref: Each application reference is APP-<date>-<time>-<hex> built from the email's received timestamp plus a random guid() tail (e.g. APP-20260626-1430-A1B2, minute precision) - UNIQUE per email even if two arrive in the same minute, and never reused even after rows are deleted or the table is cleared. detect_pattern is the case-insensitive substring that flags a reply quoting a ref; it is matched anywhere in subject OR body and the APP-... token is extracted from there. Keep it specific but decade-proof: 'app-20' covers 2000-2099. The IsKnownSender guard ignores refs from senders not already in the table. date_format sets the date portion (PA formatDateTime token); time_format is also a PA formatDateTime token (HHmm = minute precision, shorter refs; HHmmss for second precision); hex_length is how many uppercase hex chars are taken from guid() for the collision-avoidance tail. _ref_len (used to extract a quoted ref out of a reply) is computed from these same two values, so minting and extraction can never drift apart - changing either here and rebuilding keeps both in sync automatically.
_comment_spam_filters: EVERY term in every list below is matched with an UNANCHORED, case-insensitive contains() - there is no word-boundary or regex support in Power Automate. A term is therefore only safe if it cannot occur inside ordinary applicant text. bad_senders is matched against the raw From header (which may be 'Display Name <addr>'), bad_subjects against the subject, and the four content lists against subject + body + attachment filenames. Audit on 2026-07-31 replayed all 167 terms over 278 real messages: only 'marketing@' had ever fired, and all 3 hits were a genuine Chief Marketing Officer applicant (ibreathemarketing@gmail.com) whose emails were silently junked. Removed it, and narrowed five bare bad_subjects tokens that collide with real job titles ('alert' -> Alert Systems Engineer, 'invoice' -> Invoice Processing Specialist, 'receipt' -> Receipt Reconciliation Analyst, 'payment' -> Payments Platform, 'survey' -> Land Surveyor). RULE FOR NEW TERMS: prefer multi-word phrases or distinctive domains; never a bare common noun, and never a short local-part like 'marketing@'. test_p1.py locks in the specific terms already found unsafe.

your driver ai application is already

spam_filters._comment_malware_ext: Each executable extension carries a TRAILING SPACE on purpose. The scan field is 'subject + body + attachment-names', and build_zip.py appends a trailing space after the joined attachment names so every filename is space-terminated. That makes '.exe ' match the attachment 'invoice.exe' while NOT matching prose like 'www.exeter.ac.uk' (.exet) or 'www.iso.org' (.iso.) - both real false positives found on 2026-07-31. Do NOT strip these trailing spaces.
